clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. To provide additional authority to the Department of Defense and  
the Department of Transportation to respond to the continuing threat posed by  
Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait, the authority under section 673 of title 10, United  
States Code, to order any unit, and any member not assigned to a unit  
organized to serve as a unit, in the Ready Reserve to active duty (other than  
for training) for not more than 24 consecutive months, is invoked and made  
available, according to its terms, to the Secretary concerned, subject, in the  
case of the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, to the direction of  
the Secretary of Defense. The term “Secretary concerned” is defined in section  
101(8) of title 10, United States Code, to m ean the Secretary of the Army with  
respect to the Army; the Secretary of the N avy with respect to the Navy, the  
Marine Corps, and the C oast Guard when it is operating as a service in the  
Navy; the Secretary of the Air Force with respect to the Air Force; and, the  
Secretary of Transportation with respect to the C oast Guard when it is not  
operating as a service in the Navy.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. To allow for the orderly administration of personnel within the armed  
forces, the authority vested in the President by section 527 of title 10, United  
States Code, to suspend the operation of sections 523-526 of title 10, United  
States Code, regarding officer strength and officer distribution in grade, is  
invoked to the full extent provided by the terms thereof.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. To allow for the orderly administration of personnel within the armed  
forces, the authority vested in the President by section 644 of title 10, United  
States Code, to suspend the operation of any provision of law  relating to the  
promotion, involuntary retirement, or separation of commissioned officers of  
the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps, is invoked to the full extent  
provided by the terms thereof.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. The Secretary of Defense is hereby designated and empowered,  
without the approval, ratification, or other action by the President, to exercise  
the authority vested in the President by sections 527 and 644 of title 10, United  
States Code, as invoked by sections 2 and 3 of this order, to suspend the  
operation of certain provisions of law.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. The authorities delegated by sections 1 and 4 of this order may be  
redelegated and further subdelegated to civilian subordinates who are ap­
pointed to their offices by the President, by and with the advice and consent  
of the Senate.

=== PDF page 248 of 260 ===
2662 Federal Register /  V o l 56, N o. 15 ]  W ednesday, January 23, 1991 /  Presidential Documents

clauses.label: Sec. 6.
clauses.text:
Sec. 6. This order is intended to improve the internal management of the  
executive branch, and is not intended to create any right or benefit, substan­
tive or procedural, enforceable at law  by a party against the United States, its  
agencies, its officers, or any person.

clauses.label: Sec. 7.
clauses.text:
Sec. 7. This order is effective immediately, and shall be transmitted to the  
Congress and published in the Federal Register.

versions.research_rationale: EO 12743 (signed 1991-01-18, 56 FR 2661-2662), read in full from the held official FR text: preamble (NEA sec. 301; in furtherance of the EO 12722 emergency); sec. 1 invokes 10 U.S.C. 673 for the Secretaries concerned; secs. 2-3 invoke 10 U.S.C. 527 and 644; sec. 4 delegates the 527/644 authority to the Secretary of Defense; sec. 5 redelegation; sec. 6 no private rights; sec. 7 effective immediately and transmittal. It has no term or sunset. EO 13350 (preamble) revokes it in full as an order based on the EO 12722 emergency, effective 12:01 a.m. EDT 2004-07-30 (sec. 10). The dossier's 7 clauses cover secs. 1-7 with no textual gap. D6 / earlier-end test: the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds 12743 named as an order only in EO 13286 sec. 35 and EO 13350 (the other hits are pay-table figures and FR page numbers in EO 8280, 8281, 9490, 9491, 9793, 12165, 12199, 12200); OFR catalog notes record the EO 13286 amendment and the EO 13350 revocation, and the USC note at 10 U.S.C. 12302 records the same two events. The EO 13286 sec. 35 amendment (effective 2003-03-01) is attached as a later event on sec. 1; it substitutes Homeland Security for Transportation and ends nothing. No order ended or suspended any clause before 2004-07-30. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_13350 (EO 13350, 69 FR 46055-46057, read once in full; reused from Lambertini scale after re-verifying text_sha256 904607b3... on disk; Annex pages 4-13 are images): the preamble terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12722 and revokes EO 12722, 12724, 12734, 12743, 12751 and 12817 'that are based on that national emergency'; sec. 1 provides, under NEA sec. 202(a) (50 U.S.C. 1622(a)), that the termination 'shall not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date', and continues under IEEPA sec. 207(a) the blocking of property blocked under EO 12722 or 12724 only; secs. 2-8 set up new measures under the 2003 emergency (EO 13303/13315); sec. 9 disclaims private rights; sec. 10 makes the order effective at 12:01 a.m. EDT July 30, 2004. There is no transfer of functions and no exception for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 12743 in full (preamble, secs. 1-7): it invoked the 10 U.S.C. 673 Ready Reserve call-up authority for the Secretaries concerned (sec. 1, as amended by EO 13286 sec. 35 for the Coast Guard), invoked the 10 U.S.C. 527 and 644 suspension authorities (secs. 2-3), delegated them to the Secretary of Defense (sec. 4) and allowed redelegation (sec. 5). Orders to active duty issued, service performed and suspensions of officer-strength, promotion and separation laws applied before 2004-07-30 are actions taken and rights or duties matured under an order based on the EO 12722 emergency, which EO 13350 sec. 1 (NEA 202(a)) leaves unaffected. The order created no office, fund or property and no private right (sec. 6). No clause of EO 12743 continues; state transferred_or_accrued records the preserved completed effects, as in the committed claim on EO 12734 revoked by the same sentence. S1 transfer-wording prefill (review) resolved to transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: the order and the ending instrument read in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals, every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.
